subject: Discovery recap: reliability, SLOs & graceful degradation (FinPay)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability, SLOs & graceful degradation (FinPay)

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Below is a quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Recent production incident on 2026-01-12 (partial checkout failures for ~27 minutes) that led to revenue impact and manual rollback.
- Lack of deterministic failover — traffic shifts to an internal fallback that increased latency and degraded model quality.
- Internal ops complexity: multiple model variants, ad-hoc failover scripts, and limited runbook automation.

Current stack
- In-house API gateway + GKE for customer-facing services.
- Models hosted on GPUs in us-west-2 today; on-prem batch infra for heavy retraining workloads.
- No dedicated inference tier — using a mix of spot and on-demand instances.

Success criteria (what FinPay wants to measure)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for core checkout flows.
- Availability SLA: 99.9% monthly for inference endpoints.
- Graceful degradation: automated fallback to a lower-cost, lower-quality model with bounded latency (p95 < 600ms) and documented quality deltas.
- Transparent incident telemetry and post-incident runbooks available to FinPay on request.

Reliability & graceful degradation specifics we discussed
- Fallback strategy: route to a quantized / distilled model variant in the same region when primary pool is degraded; cross-region failover to us-east-1 as a secondary option.
- Circuit breakers and automatic throttling for noisy clients to protect core flows.
- KV/prefix caching to reduce cold-starts and minimize burst token costs.
- Audit logs + token-level tracing available via Redwood Console for post-incident analysis.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Send our SLA one-pager + mutual action plan (attached) — action: Marissa (today) — Done (attached).
2) Security/compliance touchpoint: schedule 30-min call with FinPay infra/security to review SOC2 scope & network requirements — action: Alyssa to propose times (next week).
3) Technical deep-dive: include your engineering lead + our runtime engineer (Rishi) to validate fallbacks and cross-region behavior — action: Marissa / Rishi to propose slots (by Mon 3/23).
4) Pricing/contract path: provide preliminary pricing for a dedicated small pool + burst capacity and procurement checklist — action: Marissa (2 business days).

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_one_pager.pdf, FinPay_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

If that aligns, I’ll get Rishi and our solutions engineer on the technical call and loop in our contracts lead for a preliminary quote.

Thanks,

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0138
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability, SLOs & graceful degradation (FinPay)

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the discussion. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) Incident detail: our SRE wanted confirmation that you can surface per-request tracing back to the failing upstream service (we need request ids and token-level traces).
2) Fallback model behavior: can you share a short benchmark or quality delta for the proposed quantized/distilled model vs our current primary? We need to understand expected impact on authorization accuracy.
3) Procurement timeline: we’re targeting a POC kickoff by 4/6. Procurement will need a preliminary quote and any required security docs (SOC2 report, IP protection language).

Also, we’d prefer dedicated capacity for the POC to avoid noisy neighbors. Can you include an example sizing/price for a "small" dedicated pool that can handle ~10 reqs/sec with p95 target?

I can schedule the security touchpoint — available Tue/Wed next week afternoons PT.

Best,
Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Engineering — Payments | FinPay
alyssa.chen@finpay.com | (650) 555-0222
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability, SLOs & graceful degradation (FinPay)

Hi Alyssa — great questions. Quick answers and next steps below. Happy to expand any item on the technical call.

1) Tracing / request ids: yes — Redwood Console can ingest and display request_id-level traces and token-level latency. We’ll provide a short runbook on how to instrument your gateway to forward request ids and correlation headers.

2) Fallback benchmarks: attached is a short benchmark snapshot (summary in the SLA one-pager) showing expected quality delta: distilled model reduces latency by ~40% with a ~2.5% drop in authorization precision on our baseline internal dataset. We recommend running your eval harness against our provided model snapshot during the POC.

3) Dedicated capacity pricing: attached is a preliminary estimate for a small dedicated pool (handles ~10 req/s with headroom for burst up to 25 req/s). We’ll include an itemized breakout in a formal quote.

Next actions I’ll take this week:
- Schedule technical deep-dive with Rishi + your infra lead (propose Tue 3/24 1pm PT and Wed 3/25 2pm PT) — action: Marissa.
- Share SOC2 summary and onboarding checklist (we’ll send the redacted SOC2 report under NDA if required) — action: Marissa.
- Prepare small dedicated pool pricing and MP (contract) template for procurement — action: Marissa (by Tue 3/23 EOD).

Links: HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/FP-6789
DocuSign (estimate): https://www.docusign.com/FP-2026-03-001/estimate

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar invites after you confirm a security touchpoint slot.

—
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability, SLOs & graceful degradation (FinPay)

Looping in Laura for pricing/contract sign-off. Marissa — I’ll take the lead on the technical deep-dive and bring a short runbook that covers: fallback model selection, cross-region failover logic, and runbook playbooks for the 2026-01-12 style incident.

Laura — will we need an approval for a promotional credit / POC discount if FinPay signs on a committed Dedicated capacity? I expect procurement will push for budget-neutral POC.

Thanks,
Rishi
